title: Hello!
text:
I am a Senior Data Manager and public health data specialist working on malaria research programs in Kenya. My work focuses on building reliable data systems, strengthening data quality, and supporting analyses that inform malaria control strategies and public health policy.
I currently support malaria research and surveillance activities through the AMPATH Malaria Program, a collaboration between Moi University, Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital, Duke University, and the Kenyan Ministry of Health. In this role, I manage large research datasets from cohorts, surveys, and clinical trials, coordinate field data collection systems, and support researchers with data preparation, monitoring, and analysis. I am also a Certified Carpentries Instructor, and my enthusiasm for teaching R and helping others build practical data skills is immeasurable.
Over the past 15+ years, I have worked across several public health programs in Kenya, contributing to the design and management of health information systems, monitoring and evaluation frameworks, and reporting tools. I have supported research and implementation projects focused on malaria surveillance, vector infectivity studies, seasonal malaria chemoprevention, and private-sector malaria case management.
My technical work involves cleaning and organizing complex health datasets, supporting statistical analysis, and developing tools that make research data easier to understand and use for informed decision-making.
My journey in data management began as a data entry clerk. With a strong attention to detail, I quickly transitioned into working with the data quality and reporting teams. This experience opened opportunities to work closely with government health systems, where I supported pharmacy supply chain programs to ensure that over 100 health facilities consistently maintained access to essential medicines and commodities.
I later transitioned fully into research data management. My early analytical work started in Excel, before moving to Stata, and eventually to R, which has become my primary tool for data analysis and reproducible research. My passion for R has also inspired me to share these skills with others. For the past five years, I have organized and taught R training sessions for data managers and public health professionals, using the Carpentries teaching model to make data analysis approachable and practical for beginners.
